o.text: Borrowed from Arabic إيضاح (ʔīḍāḥ), verbal noun of أَوْضَحَ (ʔawḍaḥa, “to make clear”).
From Proto-Turkic *kẹ̄mi (“boat”). Cognate with Crimean Tatar and Turkish gemi, Chuvash кимӗ (kimĕ) etc.
Ultimately from Latin generālis, via Russian генера́л (generál).

From uğra- (“to encounter”) + -ş, exhibiting a sound change as in o > u. For similar formation, compare oynaş.
The analysis as blend of oğru + aş has been suggested, but is likely a folk etymology.
Internationalism. Borrowed from Russian журнали́ст (žurnalíst), from French journaliste.
